parameters.note: Body weight in kg and lb alike, as a scale shows it (81.5 kg, 179.7 lb). ADR-029.
Bar and dumbbell loads; a trailing .0 is dropped (100 kg, 225 lb, 102.5 kg). ADR-029.
A tape reads to about 0.1 in / 0.5 cm; one decimal in both. ADR-029.

The server keeps body weight (NewWeighIn.kg) and load (NewSet.loadKg) to 2 decimals; a finer value is a 400. A value typed in lb is rounded here, once. parameters.test.ts checks it against the contract.
The server keeps the waist (NewWaistMeasurement.cm) to 1 decimal. parameters.test.ts checks it against the contract.
Only the default before the user chooses (onboarding asks, settings change it): the countries that use US customary units.

Evre 7: a load shown in pounds is a real one: the nearest 5 lb (a 45 lb bar with 5 lb and 2.5 lb plates, 5 lb dumbbell steps), never 209.4 lb. The engine and the server stay in kg; this is only how a load reads (loadValue and formatLoad, the one place).
Under this many lb a load is shown to the nearest 2.5 lb (small plates, light dumbbells).

A load that sits on this kilo grid (the engine's targets for a kilo gym: 2.5 kg plates in pairs) came from kilos, so a pound user reads it to the rack even where it falls near a pound by chance (110 kg is 242.51 lb). Only an off-grid load can be one typed in pounds, and that is shown as typed.
The plates a side are said in the user's unit: a user in pounds with a gym still in kilos reads the standard US rack, a 45 lb bar and these plates. Only for how the plates read; no load is changed.
The standard US plates, heaviest first.
